cards.title: Managing Kids' Meltdowns From Toddlers to Teens
cards.body: Expert parents share practical strategies for handling emotional outbursts across different ages. Meltdowns are normal child development, but they can test parents' patience and create conflict.

cards.title: Baby-Led Weaning: The Messy Reality
cards.body: A cartoon explores the increasingly popular weaning approach and its practical challenges. The piece humorously examines what parents actually deal with during the transition to solid foods.

cards.title: Don't Buy Grand Theft Auto VI for Kids
cards.body: The 18-rated game contains extreme violence, sex, and drug content unsuitable for children. Parents should understand the game's explicit nature before purchase decisions.

cards.title: Understanding PDA in Children: Anxiety or Defiance?
cards.body: New research examines whether Pathological Demand Avoidance differs from typical opposition defiant disorder. Parents should understand the science shaping diagnoses of their child's behavior.

cards.title: Teachers Need Better Left-Handedness Knowledge
cards.body: Teachers play a critical role in writing education but often lack awareness of left-handed children's specific needs. Proper training ensures these students receive appropriate support.

cards.title: Quadruplets Born in Rare One-in-700,000 Pregnancy
cards.body: A specialist team of 30 clinicians delivered the rare quadruplets after an extraordinary pregnancy. The delivery showcases modern obstetric care for complex multiple births.

cards.title: Robotic Exoskeleton Helps 7-Year-Old Walk
cards.body: A young boy with a strength-affecting condition took his first steps with cutting-edge technology. The breakthrough gave his family an emotional moment and hope for his mobility.

cards.title: ADHD and Autism Diagnoses Getting Professional Reassessment
cards.body: A Swedish government-funded clinic is re-evaluating diagnoses for people who feel they don't reflect their condition. While many find initial diagnoses affirming, reassessment offers a second look.
